rem:h3-markov-wenzl-weights-context:
Remark Scope, Borromean corollary, chirality, and notation for the H_3 Wenzl weights.

Scope — which trace, in which channel

This proposition concerns the Jones / Temperley–Lieb normalisation of the \mathrm{H}_3(q) Markov trace — the trace at Ocneanu parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) whose value on a braid closure is the Jones polynomial. Its defining feature is y_{(1^3)} \equiv 0: the Temperley–Lieb quotient annihilates the three-row partition.

Both the mass and binding channels use this trace uniformly across the framework, and the parameter is forced by the fibre decomposition: the eigenbasis decomposition for the Feynman amplitude imposes the row cap \ell(\lambda) \leq 2 inside the index set of V^{\otimes n} \cong \bigoplus V_\lambda \otimes S_\lambda, giving y_{(1^3)} = 0, and the Markov-trace selection theorem then makes z = q^3/(q^2+1) the unique faithful normalised Markov trace (entering through the Borromean Markov trace and the dressing factor F_{\mathrm{Bor}} into the nucleon mass). Independently, the Ocneanu parameter determines the fibre rank through z \cdot [N]_q = q^{N-1} q = q^N, which is injective in N for q > 1 and yields the integer rank N = 2 at z = q^3/(q^2+1). Note also the generator distinction in primitive Markov-trace axioms (M1–M4) and Categorical mass as Markov trace: the Temperley–Lieb loop reciprocal 1/\delta = 1/[2]_q evaluates the Temperley–Lieb generator e_i = q - \sigma_i, whereas under \sigma-stabilisation \mathrm{tr}_M(e_i) = q - z = 1/[2]_q gives z = q^3/(q^2+1). At q = 1 the weights reduce to (\tfrac12,\tfrac14,0), and at q_0 they evaluate to (0.5054,\,0.2473,\,0).

What writhe 0 does and does not buy. For \beta \in B_3 with writhe 0 and \pi(\beta) = \mathrm{id} both one-dimensional characters equal 1, so by the corollary below the trace depends on the weights only through y_{(2,1)}: the split between y_{(3)} and y_{(1^3)} is invisible, because normalisation \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1 already pins y_{(3)} + y_{(1^3)} = 1 - 2y_{(2,1)}. This is why the chirality asymmetry between (3) and (1^3) is unobservable on such braids. It does not make \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) independent of the Markov parameter z: two normalised Markov traces \mathrm{tr}_M, \mathrm{tr}'_M with weights y, y' agree on such a braid precisely when y_{(2,1)} = y'_{(2,1)} or \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta) = 2, and on \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} (\chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6 \neq 2 for h \neq 0),

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) - \mathrm{tr}'_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  \bigl(y_{(2,1)} - y'_{(2,1)}\bigr)\bigl(-3h^4 - h^6\bigr).

Immediate corollary — the Borromean closed form in one line

For any writhe-0 braid \beta \in B_3 with \pi(\beta) = \mathrm{id} \in S_3:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta)
  \;=\;
  1 + \frac{\chi^{(2,1)}(\beta) - 2}{[2]_q^{2}}.

The entire h-dependence of such traces is carried by the single standard-channel character; the Borromean closed form is this identity evaluated at \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6.

Non-uniformity of the weights — chirality of the Jones trace

A bar-involution argument would suggest y_{(3)} = y_{(1^3)} (the transpose pair). It fails: the transpose symmetry \lambda \leftrightarrow \lambda^T is induced by the sign-twist automorphism \sigma_i \mapsto -q\,\sigma_i^{-1}, and the Jones-normalised Markov trace is not invariant under this automorphism — it is chiral, weighting the \sigma- and \sigma^{-1}-eigenchannels asymmetrically. The extreme expression of this asymmetry is y_{(1^3)} \equiv 0 against y_{(3)}(1) = 1/2.

At q = 1 the trace reduces to the cycle-counting trace \mathrm{tr}_M(w) = 2^{\,c(w) - n} on \mathbb{C}[S_3] (c(w) = number of cycles), and Schur orthogonality reproduces (\tfrac12, \tfrac14, 0) directly.

Notation note — y_\lambda, \mu_\lambda, \chi^\lambda, w_\lambda are distinct

Four \lambda-indexed scalars appear in the Hecke-algebra blocks of this paper. They are easy to conflate by symbol similarity but encode independent data:

  • y_\lambda(q) — Wenzl/Markov coefficient: appears in \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \cdot \chi^\lambda, normalised by \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \, d_\lambda = 1. This proposition gives the Jones/Temperley–Lieb values at z = q^3/(q^2+1), for which y_{(1^3)} \equiv 0.
  • \chi^\lambda(g) — character: trace of the V_\lambda-representation on a specific element g (e.g. a braid).
  • \mu_\lambda(q) — q-Laplacian eigenvalue on V_\lambda (Peter--Weyl decomposition of the q-heat kernel (archimedean)): the heat-kernel decay rate, not a Markov-trace ingredient.
  • w_\lambda(q) = [n]_q! / H_q(\lambda)^2 — Plancherel measure (The symmetric point loses resolution, not spectrum): normalised by \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(1) = 1 at q = 1 only — the q-deformed sum \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) is not 1 (0.987 at n = 3, 1.051 at n = 8); at q = 1 it is non-uniform in a different pattern (\tfrac16, \tfrac23, \tfrac16 for n = 3) from the Wenzl weights of this proposition (\tfrac12, \tfrac14, 0).

Significance for the Borromean derivation

The 1/4 factor in h^4(\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})) = (-3) \cdot (1/4) = -3/4 is y_{(2,1)}(q = 1) = 1/[2]_q^2|_{q=1} from this proposition — and the identity y_{(2,1)}(q) = 1/[2]_q^2 holds exactly for all q, not only at the symmetric point. The Borromean h^4 separation into character coefficient \times Markov normalisation is therefore an exact structural fact, with the (h^2 + 4) denominator of the closed form being precisely [2]_q^2 = 1/y_{(2,1)}(q).

The q = 1 weights (\tfrac12, \tfrac14, 0) are not uniform, since the Jones trace is not sign-twist invariant. They are verified three ways: Schur orthogonality on the q = 1 cycle-counting trace, the exact q-dependent closed forms above, and canonical reproduction of the Borromean closed form at 30 digits.
rem:convention-d-chirality-side:
Remark The two-row Markov trace weighs the two eigenlines of a crossing unequally. Each generator \sigma_i of H_n(q) has two eigenlines: the line on which it acts by q, with projector P_+ = (\sigma_i + q^{-1})/[2]_q, and the line on which it acts by -q^{-1}, with projector P_- = (q - \sigma_i)/[2]_q. The Hecke relation fixes only q - q^{-1}, so it does not single out either line. Relabelling the root q \mapsto -q^{-1} exchanges P_+ and P_- and leaves the generator unchanged.

The two-row Markov trace selected in the Markov-trace selection, with parameter z(q) = q^3/(q^2+1), does single out a line. It does so in three ways.

  1. At n = 3 it kills the block on which every generator acts by -q^{-1}. That block is (1^3), which carries weight y_{(1^3)} = 0 (the antisymmetriser lemma). The block on which every generator acts by q is (3), and it keeps the weight y_{(3)} = (q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2.
  2. Its parameter depends on the root label. Evaluating at q gives z(q) = q^3/(q^2+1), while evaluating at -q^{-1} gives z(-q^{-1}) = -1/(q^3+q).
  3. At every level n it weighs the two lines in the ratio [3]_q : 1. For any Markov trace, \tau(P_+) = (z + q^{-1})/[2]_q and \tau(P_-) = (q - z)/[2]_q, and neither depends on n. At z = q^3/(q^2+1):
\frac{\tau(P_+)}{\tau(P_-)} \;=\; [3]_q \;=\; q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}.

This is the ratio of the quantum dimensions of \mathrm{Sym}^2 V and \Lambda^2 V for the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) fundamental V. It equals 3 at q = 1 and is unchanged under q \mapsto q^{-1}. The bias therefore comes from the two-row Markov trace itself, not from |q| > 1.

The favoured line is the one on which the generator acts by q. For q > 1 that is the line on which a positive crossing acts with eigenvalue of modulus greater than 1.

What this does not say. These are observations about a ruled trace convention. Nothing here identifies either eigenline with a physical chirality, or the favoured line with the left-handed weak coupling. That identification is not made.

The bias is also not exclusive. The algebra P_- H_n P_- (call it the corner over P_-) contains a copy of \mathfrak{sl}_2 for every n \geq 4. The z = q^3/(q^2+1) trace gives that copy zero weight at n = 4 only. From n = 5 on, both corners carry \mathfrak{sl}_2-carrying blocks with non-zero two-row weight, and the weighted share of the two corners tends to [3]_q : 1.
rem:trace-ledger:
Remark The trace ledger: four traces, one Markov trace, and where the Euler characteristic is not. Four different operations in this paper are called a trace, and the Euler characteristic of the base curve is none of them. This remark lists them once, says how they are related, and marks which relations are proved.

1. The rigid trace and the quantum dimension. In a rigid monoidal category every endomorphism f \colon X \to X has a trace \mathrm{tr}(f) \in \operatorname{End}(\mathbf{1}), obtained by closing f with the evaluation and coevaluation of X. The trace of the identity is the quantum dimension \dim_q(X). For the fundamental object of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) it is [2]_q = q + q^{-1}; for the irreducible of highest weight m - 1 it is [m]_q. On the Hecke tower this trace is what one obtains by closing a braid on one strand.

2. The Markov trace. On the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q) a Markov trace is a family of linear functionals \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_n(q) \to R that is normalised, cyclic and compatible with adding a strand at a fixed parameter z. It is a linear combination of the irreducible characters, \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda\, \chi_\lambda, and the Markov-trace selection proposition says which weights the framework uses: the row cap y_\lambda = 0 for partitions with three or more rows and y_{(n-k,k)} = [n - 2k + 1]_q / [2]_q^{\,n}, corresponding to z = q^{3}/(q^{2} + 1). Its value on a closed braid is the Jones polynomial, and its value on the identity of H_1 is 1 — after the normalisation by [2]_q^{\,n} that the weights carry, the quantum dimension of V^{\otimes n} has been divided out.

3. The Hecke characters. The \chi_\lambda themselves are the traces of the irreducible representations of H_n(q), one for each partition \lambda of n; they are the Wedderburn blocks of the algebra. Any trace on H_n(q) is a linear combination of them, so the content of a trace is its weight vector (y_\lambda).

4. The categorical trace. For a k-linear category \mathbf{C} the categorical trace, or zeroth Hochschild homology HH_0(\mathbf{C}), is the quotient of \bigoplus_X \operatorname{End}(X) by the span of the commutators fg - gf [bghl-2017]. The rigid trace of item 1 is the composite \operatorname{End}(X) \to HH_0(\mathbf{C}) \to \operatorname{End}(\mathbf{1}), and the class of \mathrm{id}_X in HH_0(\mathbf{C}) is the categorical Chern character of X. For a semisimple category with finitely many simple objects, HH_0(\mathbf{C}) is k^{\{\text{simples}\}}, so the Chern character of X is its vector of multiplicities and the rigid trace evaluates it against the vector of quantum dimensions. On a derived category of coherent sheaves the same construction gives Hochschild homology of the variety and the Mukai pairing [caldararu-willerton-2010]; on the Hecke category it gives the horizontal trace, which specialises to Markov-type traces on H_n(q) [trinh-2021].

How they are related, and what is proved. Closing the fibre action of H_n(q) on V^{\otimes n} by the categorical trace produces a Markov trace; that the row cap and faithfulness on the two-row blocks force the parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2} + 1) — is proved at n = 3 and verified numerically for every partition of n \leq 7. Whether the trace the mass channel actually uses is the categorical trace of the fibre action is the open antecedent of that proposition, and the general-n statement is proved only as fixed-n instances of the recursion [m + 2]_q + [m]_q = [2]_q [m + 1]_q. The deformation-quantisation index theorem [nest-tsygan-1995] is the model for a trace evaluated through a Chern character and a characteristic class; the paper does not yet construct the corresponding map for the aether.

Where the Euler characteristic is not. None of the four traces produces \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g. The number -6 enters the paper through the base curve — its genus, its tangent bundle's Euler class, the alternating sum of its Hochschild homology — and not through the closure of any braid (three Euler characteristics).
rem:categorical-trace-is-the-markov-trac:
Remark The rigid trace of the tensor representation is the Markov trace. The trace ledger lists the rigid trace of an endomorphism and the Markov trace on the Hecke algebra as two operations. On the tensor representation they are one operation, and this remark says in what sense.

The tensor representation. Let V be the fundamental object of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), of quantum dimension [2]_q = q + q^{-1}. The braiding gives B_n, hence the Hecke algebra H_n(q), an action on V^{\otimes n}; the generator \sigma_i acts on the i-th and (i{+}1)-st factors by the R-matrix \check{R}, which in the Hecke normalisation satisfies (\check R - q)(\check R + q^{-1}) = 0. Every endomorphism \rho(\beta), \beta \in H_n(q), has a rigid trace in \operatorname{End}(\mathbf{1}) = R: close the strands with the evaluation and coevaluation of V^{\otimes n}. Since the coevaluation of a rigid braided category with a pivotal structure is weighted, the rigid trace is the quantum trace, \mathrm{tr}(\rho(\beta)) = \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(K^{\otimes n} \rho(\beta)\bigr) with K the pivotal element [reshetikhin-turaev1990]; at \beta = 1 it returns \dim_q(V^{\otimes n}) = [2]_q^{\,n}.

The identification. Define \tau_n(\beta) = \mathrm{tr}(\rho(\beta)) / [2]_q^{\,n}. Then \tau_n(1) = 1; \tau_n is cyclic because a trace is; and closing one generator gives, by direct computation on V \otimes V,

  \tau_2(\sigma_1) \;=\; \frac{\operatorname{Tr}(K^{\otimes 2}\check R)}{[2]_q^{\,2}} \;=\; \frac{q^{3}}{q^{2} + 1} \;=\; z ,

the canonical Markov parameter. The Markov property \tau_{n}(\beta \sigma_{n-1}) = z\, \tau_{n-1}(\beta) for \beta \in H_{n-1}(q) follows by closing the last strand first: the partial quantum trace of \check R over that strand is an endomorphism of V commuting with the action, hence a scalar by Schur's lemma, and the one-generator computation identifies the scalar as z\,[2]_q. Hence \tau_n is a Markov trace with parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2} + 1), and by the uniqueness clause of the Markov-trace selection proposition it is \mathrm{tr}_M, the trace the framework uses [jones1987].

The weights, read off. Decompose V^{\otimes n} = \bigoplus_{k} V_{n-2k} \otimes S_{(n-k,k)} over the two-row partitions, with S_\lambda the irreducible H_n(q)-module of partition \lambda (the quantum Schur–Weyl duality of \mathrm{SU}_q(2)). The quantum trace of \rho(\beta) on this sum is \sum_k \dim_q(V_{n-2k})\, \chi_{(n-k,k)}(\beta) = \sum_k [n-2k+1]_q\, \chi_{(n-k,k)}(\beta), so

  \mathrm{tr}_M \;=\; \sum_{k} \frac{[n - 2k + 1]_q}{[2]_q^{\,n}}\, \chi_{(n-k,k)}, \qquad y_{(n-k,k)} = \frac{[n-2k+1]_q}{[2]_q^{\,n}}, \quad y_\lambda = 0 \text{ for } \ell(\lambda) \geq 3 ,

which are the weights the proposition states. Two of the four traces of the ledger therefore coincide on the tensor representation, and the two-row cap at z = q^{3}/(q^{2} + 1) is the statement that V is two-dimensional: a partition with three rows has no room in V^{\otimes n} [kassel1995].

What this does and does not say. It identifies the Markov trace with a rigid trace, and thereby with an evaluation of the Chern character of V^{\otimes n} at the pivotal element, divided by [2]_q^{\,n}; the quantum dimensions [m]_q in the weights are values of \dim_q on the Grothendieck group. It does not identify either trace with the Euler characteristic of the base curve, which is not a trace on H_n(q) at all.
prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse:
Proposition Minimum-Frobenius-norm collapse T_\beta = S \cdot 1 on H_n(R, q). Let H = H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra over a field R, equipped with the unique Jones–Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M : H \to R (Wenzl–Jones uniqueness theorem). Let R be ordered, q > 0, and let X \mapsto X^\dagger be the R-linear anti-involution fixing each \sigma_i. Equip H with the Frobenius form \langle X, Y \rangle_\tau := \mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot Y^\dagger). An element of minimum Frobenius norm satisfying the linear constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(T_\beta) = S for a scalar S \in R is:

\boxed{\; T_\beta = S \cdot 1_H \;}

with \| T_\beta \|^2_\tau = S^2. The minimiser is unique up to the radical of \langle\,\cdot\,,\cdot\,\rangle_\tau, which at z = q^3/(q^2+1) is the sum of the Wedderburn blocks of shapes with three or more rows.

Why the twist Y^\dagger is needed

The untwisted form \mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot Y) is not positive on H_n for n \ge 3. In H_3 take X = \sigma_1\sigma_2 - \sigma_2\sigma_1. Then \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = 0 and

\mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot X) \;=\; -\,\frac{2\,(q^4 + q^2 + 1)}{(q^2+1)^2} \;<\; 0
\qquad (q > 0),

so \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((S\cdot 1 + tX)^2\bigr) = S^2 + t^2\,\mathrm{tr}_M(X^2) is unbounded below in t and has no minimum. In the orthogonal seminormal form every \sigma_i is a real symmetric matrix, so \dagger is the blockwise transpose and \mathrm{tr}_M(X X^\dagger) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \,\| X_\lambda \|_F^2 \ge 0 because every Markov weight y_\lambda is non-negative.

Corollary — observable c_k invariance

The \mathfrak{Q}_\beta production rule extracts the Taylor coefficients c_k from \mathrm{tr}_M(T_\beta)(q). The constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(T_\beta) = S = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta / E_0 is satisfied identically under both the Euclidean L^2 coordinate norm and the canonical Markov–Frobenius norm. Then \mathrm{tr}_M(T_\beta)(q) \equiv S(q). The coefficients c_k are invariant:

c_k^{\,L^2} = c_k^{\,\mathrm{Markov}} = c_k\!\!\left(S(q)\right)
\quad\text{for all } k.

The observables are extracted from the constraint, not from the operator expansion. The norms only differ in selecting the primal-feasible operator T_\beta \in H_n(R, q).

Categorical reading

Under the Markov–Frobenius norm, T_\beta = S \cdot 1_H is a scalar multiple of the identity. The q-dependence flows entirely through S(q). There is no multi-channel SHAPE distributed across the normal-form basis. The Euclidean norm's six-channel spread is an artifact of the coordinate basis. The Markov–Frobenius minimum-norm solution is the canonical choice.
prf:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse:
Proof Proof of t beta markov frobenius collapse. Completing the square.

Let X \in H satisfy the constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S. Write the decomposition X = (X - S \cdot 1) + S \cdot 1 and expand the Frobenius norm-squared:

\| X \|^2_\tau = \mathrm{tr}_M(X X^\dagger)
              = \mathrm{tr}_M\big((X - S \cdot 1)(X - S \cdot 1)^\dagger\big)
                + S \, \mathrm{tr}_M(X + X^\dagger) - S^2 \, \mathrm{tr}_M(1).

(The scalar S \cdot 1 is central and fixed by \dagger, so (X - S \cdot 1)(X - S \cdot 1)^\dagger = X X^\dagger - S(X + X^\dagger) + S^2 \cdot 1. Since \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) = \mathrm{tr}_M(T_{w^{-1}}), the trace is \dagger-invariant, so \mathrm{tr}_M(X^\dagger) = \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S; applying linearity term by term gives the identity above.)

Substituting the Markov normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and the constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S:

\| X \|^2_\tau = \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau + 2 S^2 - S^2
             = \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau + S^2.

The twisted form is positive-semi-definite: in the orthogonal seminormal form each \sigma_i is real symmetric, so \dagger is the blockwise transpose and \| Y \|^2_\tau = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \, \| Y_\lambda \|_F^2 \ge 0, since every Markov weight y_\lambda \ge 0. Therefore

\| X \|^2_\tau \;\ge\; S^2,

with equality iff \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau = 0, i.e. iff X - S \cdot 1 vanishes on every block with y_\lambda > 0. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the blocks with y_\lambda = 0 are exactly the shapes with three or more rows, so the minimiser is S \cdot 1 up to that radical. (The untwisted form \mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot X) cannot be used: it is negative on \sigma_1\sigma_2 - \sigma_2\sigma_1 \in H_3.)

Therefore T_\beta = S \cdot 1 is a minimum-Frobenius-norm primal-feasible element, with \| T_\beta \|^2_\tau = S^2. \quad\blacksquare
prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse-ge:
Proposition Min-Frobenius-norm collapse: T_β = S · 1_A — general unital R-algebra lift of [prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse]. Let R be a strict-ordered field. Let A be a unital R-algebra. Let \tau : A \to R be an R-linear normalised trace (\tau(1) = 1, \tau(xy) = \tau(yx)). Let X \mapsto X^\dagger be an R-linear anti-multiplicative map on A ((XY)^\dagger = Y^\dagger X^\dagger) with 1^\dagger = 1 and \tau(X^\dagger) = \tau(X). Assume the twisted form is positive-semi-definite: 0 \le \tau(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) for all Y \in A. For any S \in R and X \in A satisfying \tau(X) = S:

S^2 \;\le\; \tau(X \cdot X^\dagger).

If the twisted form is non-degenerate (\tau(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) = 0 \implies Y = 0), the lower bound is attained if and only if X = S \cdot 1_A.

When A is commutative, taking X^\dagger = X recovers the untwisted statement S^2 \le \tau(X \cdot X) under positivity of \tau on squares.

Relation to the aether-model version

This proposition lifts Min-Frobenius-norm collapse: T_β = S · 1 under the canonical Markov-trace inner product on H_n(R, q) from the aether model (A = R, \tau = \mathrm{id}) to the general unital R-algebra setting, where A may be non-commutative and infinite-dimensional.

Application to the Iwahori–Hecke algebra

For A = H_n(R, q) with \tau = \mathrm{tr}_M, take \dagger to be the R-linear anti-involution fixing each \sigma_i. In the orthogonal seminormal form \mathrm{tr}_M(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \,\|Y_\lambda\|_F^2 \ge 0, so the positivity hypothesis holds. The untwisted choice \dagger = \mathrm{id} does not work for n \ge 3: \mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot X) < 0 at X = \sigma_1\sigma_2 - \sigma_2\sigma_1 \in H_3. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the twisted form is degenerate, with radical the sum of the Wedderburn blocks of shapes with three or more rows, so the minimiser

T_\beta^{\mathrm{Markov}} \;=\; S \cdot 1_H

is unique only up to that radical. The L^2-Euclidean coordinate-norm operator and the Markov-Frobenius operator both reproduce the SDP constraint. The observable c_k Taylor coefficients remain invariant.
prf:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse-gen:
Proof Proof of t beta markov frobenius collapse general.

Proof

Let R, A, \tau, S, and X be as in the statement: R an ordered field, A a unital R-algebra with unit 1_A, \tau : A \to R an R-linear map with \tau(1_A) = 1 and \tau(xy) = \tau(yx), X \mapsto X^\dagger an R-linear anti-multiplicative map with 1_A^\dagger = 1_A and \tau(X^\dagger) = \tau(X), the twisted form \tau(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) positive-semi-definite, and X \in A an element satisfying the constraint \tau(X) = S.

Step 1 — centrality of scalars. For any S \in R the element S \cdot 1_A is central in A: the compatibility of the R-action with the multiplication gives (S \cdot 1_A)\,Y = S \cdot Y = Y\,(S \cdot 1_A) for every Y \in A. In particular S \cdot 1_A commutes with X even when A is non-commutative, and (S \cdot 1_A)(S \cdot 1_A) = S^2 \cdot 1_A.

Step 2 — completing the square. By linearity and 1_A^\dagger = 1_A, (X - S \cdot 1_A)^\dagger = X^\dagger - S \cdot 1_A. Expanding with Step 1,

(X - S \cdot 1_A)(X - S \cdot 1_A)^\dagger \;=\; X \cdot X^\dagger - S \cdot X - S \cdot X^\dagger + S^2 \cdot 1_A .

Applying \tau, its R-linearity, \tau(X^\dagger) = \tau(X), and the normalisation \tau(1_A) = 1,

\tau(X \cdot X^\dagger) \;=\; \tau\bigl((X - S \cdot 1_A)(X - S \cdot 1_A)^\dagger\bigr) + 2 S\, \tau(X) - S^2 .

This identity holds for every X \in A and S \in R; neither the constraint nor positivity has been used yet.

Step 3 — imposing the constraint. Substituting \tau(X) = S into the identity of Step 2,

\tau(X \cdot X^\dagger) \;=\; \tau\bigl((X - S \cdot 1_A)(X - S \cdot 1_A)^\dagger\bigr) + S^2 .

Step 4 — the lower bound. By positivity of the twisted form, \tau\bigl((X - S \cdot 1_A)(X - S \cdot 1_A)^\dagger\bigr) \ge 0, so Step 3 gives

S^2 \;\le\; \tau(X \cdot X^\dagger) ,

which is the asserted bound.

Step 5 — the equality case. Assume in addition that the twisted form is non-degenerate, i.e. \tau(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) = 0 implies Y = 0.

If \tau(X \cdot X^\dagger) = S^2, then Step 3 forces \tau\bigl((X - S \cdot 1_A)(X - S \cdot 1_A)^\dagger\bigr) = 0, so non-degeneracy applied to Y = X - S \cdot 1_A gives X - S \cdot 1_A = 0, i.e. X = S \cdot 1_A.

Conversely, if X = S \cdot 1_A, then X^\dagger = S \cdot 1_A and X \cdot X^\dagger = S^2 \cdot 1_A by Step 1, hence \tau(X \cdot X^\dagger) = S^2\, \tau(1_A) = S^2 (and the constraint \tau(X) = S \, \tau(1_A) = S holds automatically).

Therefore the lower bound S^2 is attained exactly at X = S \cdot 1_A. \blacksquare

The implications (1)--(2) are the standard passage from a q-holonomic generating function to a q-recursive coefficient sequence (coefficients polynomial in q^n) and its confluent (differential) limit; they hold for any such R. What is open is the existence and identity of the kernel R for the binding G. By the precision-floor obstruction — the c_k information bound, which makes term data unmeasurable beyond low order — R cannot be fixed by fitting the B_n; it must be derived from the fibre root-of-unity singularity structure of the Seiberg--Witten differential (The Seiberg–Witten period is an algebraic residue sum). This is the same q-difference machinery as the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision ladder, applied to the binding series.

Scope of the rank-1 hypothesis — unsatisfiable on both proposed carriers; the proposition survives only in rank 2. The supposition above is a first-order (rank-1) q-difference relation. Two carriers have been proposed for G, and neither admits one.

The raw carrier — the ordinary generating function of the raw body terms B_n = I(n)/n — was excluded by the confluent/Gevrey growth argument (proved). That exclusion explicitly re-targeted the conjecture at the q-Borel / Gevrey-normalized carrier b_n = f_n/[n]_q!, predicting depth d = 2. The normalized carrier provably satisfies [m+2]_q\,b_{m+2} = b_{m+1} + b_m, i.e. the operator L_{\mathcal{K}} = (q^2x-1)\sigma^2 - (q-1)\sigma - (q-1).

A scalar kernel is a first-order right factor \sigma - a of L_{\mathcal{K}}, i.e. a solution a\in K(x) of the q-Riccati equation (q^2x-1)\,a(qx)\,a(x) - (q-1)\,a(x) - (q-1) = 0. Writing a = P/Q and clearing denominators, the three terms have degrees 1+2p, p+u and 2u with p = \deg P, u = \deg Q. The first is odd-shaped and the third even, so 1+2p = 2u is impossible over \mathbb{Z}; a two-line case split then gives that the maximum is attained exactly once for every (p,u), and a lone top-degree term cannot cancel. Hence no rational a exists, \mathcal{K} is irreducible of rank 2, and no nonzero solution of L_{\mathcal{K}} obeys any scalar relation G(qx) = R(q,x)G(x) with R \in K(x) — a fortiori none with R\in\mathbb{Q}(q)[x,x^{-1}] of any depth d; the depth never enters the argument, only the degrees do. This exclusion is proved.

Scope (b), structural exclusion, invariant cited. The parity is the Newton-slope invariant: L_{\mathcal{K}} is pure isoclinic of slope \tfrac12 at infinity, every rank-1 q-difference module has integer slope, and Newton slopes are additive on sub- and quotient modules. Independently corroborated by the van der Put--Reversat classification of pure modules [vanderput-reversat2007, vanderput2006]: a pure module of non-integral slope d/r, \gcd(d,r)=1, and rank r is E(r,d,b) in Bugeaud's notation [bugeaud2011], and it is irreducible.

What survives. Implications (1)--(2) are unaffected and the depth-2 prediction stands — but depth 2 means rank 2: the kernel is a 2\times2 matrix A(q,x) acting on (G, \sigma G), whose \tau-image is a first-order two-component system, which is what "Dirac-type" already asks for. Restated in rank 2 the proposition is intact; restated in rank 1 it is vacuous. The exclusion is over K(x): after a degree-2 ramified base change (adjoining q^{1/2}, x^{1/2}) the slope becomes the integer 1 and a scalar kernel does exist on the double cover, relating half-shifts — that is, even and odd body orders separately. That ramification is the missing structure, not a gap in the argument.

Geometric target of the kernel module (literature). Fix q\in\mathbb{C} with 0<|q|<1 and let K=\mathbb{C}(\{z\}) be the field of germs of meromorphic functions at 0, with \varphi(z)=qz. Van der Put and Reversat show that a q-difference module M over K induces functorially a vector bundle v(M) on the Tate curve \mathbb{C}^{*}/q^{\mathbb{Z}}, for all slopes, and recover Atiyah's classification of indecomposable bundles on that curve as a corollary [vanderput-reversat2007, Introduction, §2]. Two points of convention apply before this is used here. First, the kernel module \mathcal{K} above is stated over K(x) with q an indeterminate and its slope is read at x=\infty, so the functor applies only after q is specialised to a complex number with |q|\neq 1 and the module is passed to germs at a point; for |q|>1, as at the aether value q_0, one replaces (q,\Phi) by (q^{-1},\Phi^{-1}), which leaves the lattice q^{\mathbb{Z}}, and so the curve, unchanged. Second, the Tate curve \mathbb{C}^{*}/q^{\mathbb{Z}} is not the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q of the Descartes elliptic curve; the symbol \mathcal{E}_q keeps that meaning, and the bundle v(\mathcal{K}) itself is not constructed in this paper.
prf:binding-genfun-qdifference:
Proof Proof of the q-difference recurrence of the binding generating function. Write G(x;q)=\sum_{n\geq 0}B_n x^n and, for polynomial R, R(q,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{d} r_j(q)\,x^{j}. The coefficient of x^{n} in G(qx;q) is q^{n}B_{n}, and in R(q,x)G(x;q) it is \sum_{j=0}^{d} r_j B_{n-j}. Hence

  (q^{n} - r_0)\,B_{n} \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{d} r_j\,B_{n-j},

and for q^n \neq r_0 this solves for B_n in terms of B_{n-1},\dots,B_{n-d} with coefficients r_j/(q^n - r_0), rational in q and q^n. A Laurent R shifts the indices but leaves the factor q^n on the B_n coefficient. This is the standard fact that a q-holonomic series has q-recursive coefficients; it fixes every term from R and the first d terms. (Note that the factor q^n makes the recurrence coefficients r_j/(q^n - r_0) depend explicitly on the index n, rather than being constant in n.)

For the Archimedean image, apply \tau at q=q_0 and let q\to q_0 act on the shift operator x\mapsto qx: the multiplicative q-shift degenerates to the infinitesimal generator x\,\partial_x (the confluent limit of a q-difference operator), so G(qx;q)=R(q,x)G(x;q) passes to a linear differential equation x\,\partial_x \widehat{G} = \rho(x)\,\widehat{G} on the realised \widehat{G}=\tau G — the Dirac-type equation. Given the depth-d recurrence, with position-dependent coefficients, the term identity follows; the existence of R for the binding G is the conjectural input (carried as a hypothesis). \qquad\blacksquare

prop:delta-lambda-dt-index-unification:
Proposition \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda is a DT/3d-index Euler characteristic with geometric chirality. Let \lambda be a partition, written as a weakly decreasing list, with a-function grade n(\lambda) and Wedderburn dimension \dim V_\lambda. Set

  \Delta_\lambda \;=\; (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\,\dim V_\lambda .

Then both factors are identified with independently-defined objects:

  1. (value) the DT / 3d-index Euler characteristic on the graded pieces equals \Delta_\lambda,
  \sum_{k=0}^{n(\lambda)} (-1)^k \dim \mathrm{gr}_k
  \;=\; (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\,\dim V_\lambda ;
  1. (chirality) the a-function parity equals the geometric longest-element sign,
  (-1)^{n(\lambda)} \;=\; (-1)^{\sum_i \binom{\lambda'_i}{2}} ,

where \lambda' is the conjugate partition. Both hold for every n, with no restriction.

Why this is a theorem and not a definition

Writing \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda by itself asserts nothing — it names a product of a sign and a dimension. The content is that neither factor is free:

  • the magnitude is forced as an Euler characteristic, an alternating sum over the graded pieces, rather than being posited as the Wedderburn dimension;
  • the sign is forced as a geometric invariant — the longest-element sign of the associated Weyl-group datum — rather than being posited as the jet-order parity.

The bridge between the two readings of the sign is the combinatorial identity n(\lambda) = \sum_i \binom{\lambda'_i}{2}, which is what removes the earlier n \le 5 restriction: the chirality leg had been established only for small n until that identity was proved in general.

Scope — the value only

This fixes the per-partition value. It does not address the many-body binding magnitude, which remains open: no per-block weight converts an intensive quantity into an extensive one, so the missing contribution is a separate additive extensive term rather than a different choice of \Delta_\lambda. Six closure ansätze have failed on the deuteron for exactly that reason. Nothing here should be read as narrowing that gap.
rem:springer-fibre-convention-scope:
Remark Prior art: Springer's correspondence and the convention behind the sign of \Delta_\lambda. For G = GL_n and a unipotent element x with Springer fibre \mathcal{B}_x of dimension d_x, Springer's theorem identifies the top cohomology H^{2d_x}(\mathcal{B}_x) with an irreducible representation V_\lambda of S_n, where \lambda is the Jordan type of x, under the normalisation in which V_{(n)} is the trivial and V_{(1^n)} the sign representation [shoji2019, Thm 2.1 and eq. (2.1), \S 2, pp. 3--4]. The same survey uses the statistic n(\lambda) = \sum_i (i-1)\lambda_i [shoji2019, eq. (6.3), \S 6], which is the grade n(\lambda) of the unification proposition.

What this gives here. The two factors of \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)} \dim V_\lambda behave differently under the choice of convention:

  • the magnitude is convention-free, since \dim V_\lambda = \dim V_{\lambda'};
  • the sign depends on whether \lambda or its conjugate \lambda' labels V_\lambda, because n(\lambda) \neq n(\lambda') in general.

Under Shoji's normalisation the sign is the parity of the Springer-fibre dimension, (-1)^{n(\lambda)} = (-1)^{d_x} for x of Jordan type \lambda. This is checked at the two ends of the dominance order. For \lambda = (n), x is regular, \mathcal{B}_x is a point, n(\lambda) = 0, and the representation is trivial. For \lambda = (1^n), x = 1, \mathcal{B}_x is the whole flag variety of dimension n(n-1)/2 = n(1^n), and the representation is the sign. The general equality d_x = n(\lambda) is standard, but the survey cited does not state it, so it is not attributed to that source here.

What it does not supply. The proof of the unification proposition does not use this citation; the Springer reading is an interpretation of its sign, not an input to its proof. It also does not bear on the many-body binding magnitude, which that proposition leaves open.
conj:cyclotomic-boundary-at-keystone:
Conjecture The Habiro-tail cyclotomic boundary sits at the quintic order: D(n) is cyclotomic \iff n \leq 5. The binding q-deformation of the na-Stokes period S(n) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim_q(\lambda) satisfies the recurrence

S(n) \;=\; S(n-1) \;+\; [n-1]_q\,S(n-2) \;+\; D(n),

whose deviation term D(n) — the Habiro tail — carries a universal (q-1)^2 double root at q=1 and is bar-even (D(1/q)=D(q)). The conjecture asserts that D(n) is cyclotomic — a product of cyclotomic polynomials (times the (q-1)^2 factor and a q-monomial) — if and only if n \leq 5, where 5 is the quintic order S_5 \supset A_5.

The alignment. The cyclotomic-pure regime n \leq 5 coincides exactly with the framework's calibration orders and the quintic order:

\{\,n \leq 5 : D(n)\text{ cyclotomic}\,\}
\;=\;
\underbrace{\{n=2,3,4\}}_{\text{calibration orders } c=1,2,3}
\;\cup\;
\underbrace{\{n=5\}}_{S_5\text{ quintic order}}.

The first non-cyclotomic (non-q-holonomic) content appears at the first body order n=6 that is neither a calibration nor the quintic order.

The arithmetic mechanism. At q=1 one has S(n)|_{q=1} = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} f^\lambda = I(n), the involution / telephone numbers (OEIS A000085; the Frobenius–Schur identity, proved for all n by RSK: involutions \leftrightarrow SYT). So S(n) is the q-deformed involution number — a Rogers–Szegő / q-Hermite moment — and the recurrence above is the q-lift of I(n)=I(n-1)+(n-1)I(n-2), with D(n) its deviation. Prior analysis of this q-involution kernel establishes the tail's structure: a (q-1)^2 double root times a bar-even cofactor that is cyclotomic through n=5 and acquires a genuine non-cyclotomic, non-q-holonomic factor from n=6 — the same non-holonomicity that obstructs any fixed-order closed form for S(n). This is the mechanism that governs D(n): it is a property of cancellation in the alternating sum, not of any individual quantum dimension.

Why the individual quantum dimensions do not locate the boundary. Every \dim_q(\lambda) = [n]_q!/\prod_c [h(c)]_q is a product of cyclotomic polynomials for every n (a ratio of cyclotomic products that is a polynomial). So cyclotomic-purity of the individual dimensions does not distinguish n=5 from n=6: at both orders all \dim_q(\lambda) are cyclotomic. In particular the McKay observation below — that at n=5 the four classes carry single quantum integers while at n=6 most are compound products of several [m]_q — is a single-[m]_q-vs-product distinction, not a cyclotomic-vs-non-cyclotomic one (a product of several cyclotomics is still cyclotomic). It does not, by itself, supply the arithmetic mechanism above.

The McKay coincidence (rep-theory, link unproven). At the quintic order n=5 the four conjugation classes \{\lambda,\lambda'\} of S_5 carry quantum dimensions equal to the E_8 Coxeter marks [\mathrm{mark}]_q:

\dim_q(5)=[1]_q,\quad
\dim_q(4,1)=[4]_q,\quad
\dim_q(3,2)=[5]_q,\quad
\dim_q(3,1,1)=[5]_q+1,

because A_5 \cong 2I/\{\pm 1\} is the icosahedral group and 2I \leftrightarrow \widehat{E}_8 (McKay). The McKay–ADE ladder of alternating groups is finite: A_4 \cong tetrahedral (2T \leftrightarrow \widehat{E}_6), A_5 \cong icosahedral (2I \leftrightarrow \widehat{E}_8), and A_6 \cong \mathrm{PSL}(2,9) is not a binary polyhedral group. Thus A_5 is the last alternating group that is the rotation group of a Platonic solid, and A_6 (n=6) is the first non-McKay. That the McKay-mark structure exits at the same order the tail leaves the cyclotomic ring is a coincidence of orders; by the caveat above it does not act through cyclotomic-purity of the dimensions, and its bearing on the arithmetic mechanism is unproven.

Status — three tiers of correlation, not to be conflated.

  1. Arithmetic (the substance): D(n) is non-cyclotomic from n=6. This is proved for 6 \le n \le 20 (finite Lean certificates) and for the families n = T_j \pm 1 but not for all n \geq 6; the cofactor's non-q-holonomic degree growth is the structural reason, not yet a proof. Generic high-degree bar-even integer polynomials are non-cyclotomic, so non-cyclotomicity is the expected outcome — the content is entirely that n \leq 5 are cyclotomic, and that "for all n \geq 6, with no exceptions" is what a proof must supply.
  2. Alignment: that boundary coincides with {calibration \cup quintic} orders \{2,3,4\}\cup\{5\}.
  3. Rep-theory: the McKay-mark / S_6-outer-automorphism coincidence at n=6.

The causation — whether the A_5 \to A_6 McKay exit or the S_6 outer automorphism forces the boundary — is unproved, and the route through the single-vs-compound quantum dimensions does not establish it. What can be said is the dovetail with S(n)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\dim_q(\lambda)= \sum_\lambda W_\lambda: the same S_5 whose quantum dimensions are the E_8 marks carries the Verlinde measure W_\lambda. Specific root magnitudes are not interpreted.

What is proved. Derived from the definition (Lean, QOU.Mass.CyclotomicBoundaryCertified): for 2 \le n \le 9, over a generic field with the hook brackets nonzero, the hook-length definition above gives q^{m_n}D(n) = P_n(q) for an explicit P_n \in \mathbb{Z}[q]. In particular D(2) = D(3) = 0, D(4) = q^{-2}\Phi_1^2\Phi_3 and D(5) = 2q^{-4}\Phi_1^2\Phi_2^2\Phi_3\Phi_6, so the forward direction holds for every n \le 5. The converse through n = 20: for 6 \le n \le 20, P_n is not c\,q^j\prod_k\Phi_k. The certificate is finite integer arithmetic: if P = c\,q^j\prod\Phi_k and p \mid P(a), p \nmid a, p \nmid P(b), then a^k \equiv 1 \pmod p for some factor \Phi_k, so the order m of a mod p divides k and \varphi(m) \le \varphi(k) \le \deg P. One witness (p, a) with \varphi(m) > \deg P_n per n refutes the factorisation (for example n = 6: p = 47, a = 28, m = 23, \varphi(23) = 22 > 14). This uses no analysis and no discriminant. The polynomials P_{10}, \dots, P_{20} in the certificate are computed by computations/cyclotomic_boundary_certificates.py; for n \le 9 they are derived in Lean. The earlier n = 6 route (the deg-8 core C_6, palindrome identity, \mathrm{disc}(\tilde C) = -44208 < 0) remains proved in QOU.Mass.CyclotomicBoundaryKeystone.

Two infinite families (pen-and-paper proof, 2026-11-27). Write n = T_j + r with T_j = j(j+1)/2 and 1 \le r \le j+1.

Leading coefficient. \dim_q(\lambda) = q^{-e_\lambda}g_\lambda(q^2) is bar-even with leading coefficient 1, where e_\lambda = \binom n2 - \sum_{(i,j)\in\lambda}(i+j). The minimisers of \sum(i+j) fill the antidiagonals 0,\dots,j-1 (the staircase \delta_j) and put r cells on antidiagonal j, whose j+1 positions are all addable corners of \delta_j. So the top coefficient of S(n) is \binom{j+1}{r}. Let d_k be the antidiagonal of the k-th cell in this filling. The top degrees of S(n-1) and [n-1]_qS(n-2) lie below that of S(n) by n-1-d_n \ge 2 and by n-1-d_n-d_{n-1}, which is \ge 1 for n \ge 7. Hence, for n \ge 7,

\operatorname{lead}(P_n) = \binom{j+1}{r}.

The divisibility test. If P_n = c\,q^k\prod\Phi_{k_i}, then c = \operatorname{lead}(P_n) divides every coefficient of P_n, because each \Phi_k is monic in \mathbb Z[q].

Second coefficient. The shapes with \sum(i+j) one above the minimum are of two kinds: one cell moved from antidiagonal j to j+1, or one cell moved from j-1 to j. Counting them gives, whenever the gap n-1-d_n-d_{n-1} is \ge 2 (true for n \ge 9),

a_1(P_n) = N_1 = 2\binom{j}{r-2} + j\binom{j-1}{r-3} + j\binom{j-1}{r+1}.

This agrees with the exact P_n for 9 \le n \le 24.

  • n = T_{j+1} - 1 (r = j), every j \ge 3: N_1 = j^2(j-1)/2, and j^2(j-1) \equiv -2 \pmod{j+1}, so (j+1) \nmid N_1. D(n) is not cyclotomic.
  • n = T_j + 1 (r = 1), every j \ge 4 with j \ne 5: N_1 = j(j-1)(j-2)/2, and j(j-1)(j-2) \equiv -6 \pmod{j+1}, so (j+1) \nmid N_1 unless (j+1) \mid 6. D(n) is not cyclotomic. (The exception j = 5 is n = 16, covered by the finite certificate.)

Together with the finite certificates this settles 6 \le n \le 20, and every n \in \{T_j + 1, T_{j+1} - 1\} with j \ge 4. For other non-triangular n the second coefficient can be divisible by the leading one (at n = 16 and n = 18), so a deeper coefficient is needed. At triangular n (6, 10, 15, 21, \dots) the leading coefficient is 1 and this test gives nothing.

Open: non-cyclotomicity for every n \ge 6: all triangular n, and the non-triangular n outside the two families above n = 20.

prop:brunnian-binding-channel:
Proposition The binding multiplier is the unsigned coordination count, not a Gauss linking number: forced by Brunnian topology and bar-parity. Let a nuclear composite be assembled from component knots whose pairwise inter-component linking pattern is Brunnian — every pairwise Gauss linking number vanishes, as for the Borromean carrier \mathrm{L6a4} of {}^3\mathrm{He}/{}^4\mathrm{He}. Then the mutual binding contribution to the crossing energy is carried entirely by the sign-blind coordination-count channel, and the signed linking-number channel is identically zero. Consequently the binding multiplier is an unsigned coordination count, complementary in bar-parity to the bar-even mass self-trace, and can never coincide with it.

Setup

Write the mutual (inter-component) crossing energy of a component pair with n_+ positive and n_- negative crossings in the Skein-signed form n_+ q - n_- q^{-1}. The proved decomposition of crossing energy splits it into two channels:

  \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-)(q + q^{-1})}_{\text{signed (strong, }\cosh\text{) channel}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ + n_-)(q - q^{-1})}_{\text{unsigned (Coulomb, }\sinh\text{) channel}} .

The signed multiplicity is the writhe n_+ - n_- = 2\,\mathrm{lk}, the Gauss linking number; the unsigned multiplicity is the crossing count n_+ + n_-, a coordination count.

The Brunnian channel

A Brunnian pair has vanishing pairwise linking number, \mathrm{lk} = 0, i.e. n_+ = n_-. The signed channel then vanishes and the entire mutual/binding energy is the unsigned count channel; for a crossing pair at an aether modulus q > 1 this channel is strictly positive. So the binding energy is nonzero even where the pairwise linking number is zero — the coordination count, not the Gauss linking number, is the correct binding carrier for a Brunnian nuclear link. A minimal Brunnian bond (n_+ = n_- = 1, the pairwise pattern inside \mathrm{L6a4}) contributes exactly one coordination unit, so a fully coordinated cluster carries \binom{A}{2} units and per-nucleon z = A - 1; which pairs bond is the coordination-graph question, saturation-limited for heavy A (the complete graph is excluded there).

The deuteron sits at the boundary. What coincides there is the two multiplicities — the writhe n_+ - n_- = 2\,\mathrm{lk} and the crossing count n_+ + n_-, which are what play the role of the binding multiplier — not the channel values, whose \cosh and \sinh weights differ at every q. The two multiplicities agree exactly on all-positive carriers, n_- = 0, and the positive Hopf link is such a carrier (n_+ = 2, n_- = 0, giving |\mathrm{lk}| = 1 and coordination z = 1, both multiplicities equal to 2). On a Brunnian carrier n_+ = n_- instead, collapsing the signed multiplicity to 0 while the unsigned one is the full crossing count. So the two invariants agree for a Hopf-bonded pair and diverge from A \geq 3, where only the unsigned count is non-vanishing.

Why the assignment is forced — bar-parity

Under the bar-involution q \mapsto q^{-1} the count (binding) channel is bar-odd, while the mass self-trace \mathrm{lw} = \tfrac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda \vdash c+1} \dim_q \lambda is bar-even — every quantum dimension satisfies \dim_q = \dim_{q^{-1}} (for the fundamental [2]_q = q + q^{-1}). A nonzero bar-even function is never bar-odd, so a binding multiplier and a mass multiplier occupy complementary bar-parity sectors and can never be the same object. This is the same \cosh/\sinh split the framework uses for the bar-even meson scale and its bar-odd Q_\beta partner. The assignment mass \leftrightarrow self-trace, binding \leftrightarrow coordination count is therefore a parity fact, not a modelling choice.

Scope

The channel structure, the Brunnian reduction, the coordination-unit map for minimal bonds, and the bar-parity orthogonality are proved. The two further residuals are now also settled. The mass \leftrightarrow self, binding \leftrightarrow mutual assignment is a theorem of the crossing partition plus the mass-deficit definition of binding (B = \sum_i m_i^{\text{isolated}} - m^{\text{assembly}} = -(\text{mutual energy}); the self energies cancel), so binding is exactly the inter-component pairing ; and the crossing-count \to coordination coefficient is \tfrac{1}{2}\lvert\text{inter-crossings}\rvert in general, giving \binom{A}{2} units and per-nucleon z = A-1 for a complete graph of minimal single clasps. This is the discrete counterpart of the unsigned-invariant resolution reached independently on the electromagnetic-linking side. The additive partition lifts to the mass observable — whose self carrier is the multiplicative q-dimension Markov self-trace \mathrm{lw} — through the archimedean functor \tau = \log: a multiplicative amplitude has an additive free energy E = \log T, so the mass-deficit binding equals the connected (interaction) free energy -\log I, which is positive exactly when the assembly amplitude is suppressed.

Two multiplicative structures must be kept apart here. prop:jet-filtration-binding-extensive:
Proposition The jet-filtration binding is extensive (monotone in body order). Stated over \mathbb{R} (archimedean regime); the combinatorial content is a finite non-negative sum.

Proposition (extensivity of the body-order binding). Write the jet-filtration binding of Binding many-body series equals the jet-order filtration: B(K)=\sum_n m_e\,a_D^{(n)} as

  B(A) \;=\; \sum_{n=2}^{A} \mathfrak{m}_e \, a_D^{(n)} \, w_n ,

with \mathfrak{m}_e \geq 0, and a_D^{(n)} \geq 0, w_n \geq 0 for every body order n. Then B is monotone non-decreasing in the body-order cutoff A:

  A \leq A' \;\Longrightarrow\; B(A) \leq B(A') ,

and it is strictly increasing whenever a new body order contributes positively: if \mathfrak{m}_e\, a_D^{(A+1)}\, w_{A+1} > 0 (and A+1 \geq 2), then B(A) < B(A+1).

Adding nucleon body orders can only increase binding. This is exactly the extensive behaviour the intensive rotation-phase reading \theta_\lambda = \arccos(\chi^\lambda/d_\lambda) structurally lacked — a bounded per-block phase cannot grow with the nucleon number A (a one-parameter closure on that reading fails numerically). The body-order series supplies it, because each term \mathfrak{m}_e a_D^{(n)} w_n is a non-negative contribution and the number of terms grows with A.

The proof is elementary — monotonicity of a finite sum of non-negative terms over the nested index sets \{2,\ldots,A\} \subseteq \{2,\ldots,A'\}.

Scope (what is not asserted here). The three deeper inputs are carried as non-negativity/positivity hypotheses on a_D^{(n)} and w_n, not derived in this proposition:

  1. the super-exponential magnitude of the Seiberg–Witten period a_D^{(n)} = \oint_{\mathcal{S}_c}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} — the quantitative extensive channel;
  2. the non-abelian-Stokes identity a_D^{(n)} = \mathrm{lw}(n-1) (the mean quantum dimension; conjectural, with residue-sum form the Seiberg–Witten period is an algebraic residue sum);
  3. the per-atom residue weight w_n(K) (the \rho\cdot A scale rule, a q-difference recursion output).

What is established is the qualitative extensivity: given non-negative period and weight data, the body-order binding grows with A.

Status of (1)–(3) elsewhere in the corpus. Being carried as a hypothesis here is not the same as being open, and only one of the three now is. Item (2) is open: it is stated as a conjecture and remains unproved. Item (1) is settled as a growth class — the period is super-exponential by the \surd-branch argument of the colour cubic, confirmed independently by the residue-sum route, and the object is identified as the q-deformed involution number T_q(n) = n\,\mathrm{lw}(n-1) \to I(n); what remains open there is the exact q-statistic, for which no q-holonomic recurrence exists at low depth. prop:tower-geometric-lower-bound:

  \tfrac{1}{30}\,\bigl(\sqrt{2}\bigr)^{k} \;\leq\; w_{\mathrm{std}}(k) \qquad (k \geq 3).

Why the statement carries a threshold. Below k = 3 the weight is exactly zero, not small: no Young diagram of fewer than three cells contains (2,1), and the skew count f^{\lambda/\mu} is defined to vanish off containment. So k \geq 3 is the whole range on which any positive lower bound is possible, and a bound asserted for every k is false rather than open.

The geometric form is a weaker shadow of what is proved. The underlying result is the square bound k!/(81 \cdot 2^{k}) \leq w_{\mathrm{std}}(k)^{2}, valid for k \geq 3, which is genuinely super-exponential since k!/2^{k} outgrows every geometric sequence. The constants r = \sqrt{2} and c = 1/30 above are one convenient pair extracted from it, chosen so that the threshold falls at k = 3; the measured growth is far stronger, with successive ratios rising 1.38 \to 2.88 over k \leq 10.
prop:level-selection-not-linear:
Proposition Linear level-selection is excluded (exponential beats linear). Let w = w_{\mathrm{std}} be the branched brane-tower weight, which by Brane-tower growth above the containment threshold (GAP-A-3) satisfies c\,r^{k} \leq w(k) for k \geq 3 with r = \sqrt{2} > 1 and c = 1/30 > 0. If the binding is extensive — w(A) \leq M \cdot A for every A \geq 1 — then a contradiction follows. Consequently no linear level-selection rule k(A) = A (nor bond-count k(A) = A(A-1)/2, a fortiori) is consistent with extensive binding: the selected jet level grows at most logarithmically in A.

Proof idea. The tower bound gives c\,r^{A} \leq w(A) \leq M\cdot A for all A \geq 1. But a geometric c\,r^{A} with r > 1 eventually outgrows any linear M\cdot A — formally (A) = o(r^{A}) as A \to \infty — so the inequality cannot hold for all A. Dividing the surviving bound by c and taking \log_r shows k(A) \leq \log_r\!\big((M/c)\,A\big), i.e. at most logarithmic growth.

Restriction of the hypothesis to A \geq 1. Extensivity is imposed only for A \geq 1, the physical regime. Excluding A = 0 ensures the exclusion is the genuine growth argument rather than a degenerate boundary coincidence: at A = 0 the linear side is M \cdot 0 = 0, so the inequality would fail or hold for reasons unrelated to the exponential-versus-linear mechanism.

The tower bound does not force w(0) \geq c > 0: w_{\mathrm{std}}(0) = 0, because no diagram of fewer than three cells contains (2,1). Stated for every k, the growth hypothesis would be false at k = 0, so the A = 0 case is a falsity in the antecedent rather than a boundary effect in the conclusion. That is why Brane-tower growth above the containment threshold (GAP-A-3) now carries a threshold, and why this proposition is unconditional rather than conditional.
prop:linear-chain-bond-count:
Proposition The jet-filtration multiplicity is the linear-chain bond count M_n = n-1. The canonical atomic braid is a linear chain of A nucleon blocks (consecutive blocks joined by a single inter-nucleon crossing). Consequently, in the body-order (jet-filtration) binding Binding many-body series equals the jet-order filtration: B(K)=\sum_n m_e\,a_D^{(n)},

  • the number of consecutive n-nucleon sub-clusters is A-n+1, and
  • each n-nucleon sub-chain carries exactly n-1 inter-nucleon bonds,

so the body-order multiplicity is the bond count M_n = n-1. The aggregate bond-weighted cluster measure of the A-chain is the tetrahedral (binomial) number

  \sum_{n=2}^{A} (A-n+1)\,(n-1)
  \;=\; \binom{A+1}{3}
  \;=\; \frac{(A-1)\,A\,(A+1)}{6}.

Reindexed by k = n-1 this is \sum_{k=0}^{A-1}(A-k)\,k, and the identity follows by induction on A.

prop:alpha-cluster-activation-gate:
Proposition The \alpha-cluster activation gate: Milnor indeterminacy, sign-rep obstruction, and \mathrm{Vol}=0 annihilation. Let a three-cluster arrangement carry pairwise linking numbers (\ell_{12},\ell_{13},\ell_{23})\in\mathbb{Z}^3, and let \Delta = \gcd(\ell_{12},\ell_{13},\ell_{23}).   2. (Brunnian gate open) the residue space is the full \mathbb{Z} (the gate is open, \Delta = 0) iff all pairwise linkings vanish, \ell_{12}=\ell_{13}=\ell_{23}=0 — the Brunnian/Borromean pattern;
  3. (sign-representation obstruction) any \Sigma_3-equivariant linear map from the pair-vector module to the sign representation is identically zero over any commutative ring; the inter-cluster coupling therefore factors through |\bar\mu| only (no chirality-odd channel);
  4. (\mathrm{Vol}=0 annihilation) the W-plane binding term \mathfrak{m}_e\,\mathrm{Vol}\,q on a bond channel of hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}=0 is identically zero.

Hopf-linked spectator pairs (1) are switched off. This is the categorical origin of the "k\ge 3, \alpha-only" activation pattern: two \alpha-clusters share a Hopf-type spectator link (gate closed), whereas a Borromean triple of \alpha-clusters opens the gate.

All four parts are proved, over a generic commutative ring where the statement permits. The companion CAL-3 class-selection statement for part (4) is a conditional result: it depends on a binding-volume ledger that is an open input, not part of this proposition's proved content.

\bar\mu_{ijk} \equiv m_{ijk}(F) - t_{ijk}(F) \pmod{\delta},

where t_{ijk}(F) is the signed count of triple points of F and m_{ijk}(F) is read off from how the double curves meet the boundaries [mellor-melvin2003, Theorem, p. 561]. When the boundary of F misses the double-point set, which is possible only if all pairwise linking numbers vanish, this reduces to Cochran's formula \bar\mu_{ijk} = -t_{ijk}(F), a pure signed triple-point count [mellor-melvin2003, p. 562].

This gives the open case of the activation gate, the Brunnian pattern with all pairwise linkings zero, a surface-level object to count, in addition to the braid-word definition. The corpus's cluster arrangements are given as contact graphs and braid words, not yet realised as links with chosen Seifert surfaces, so the formula cannot be applied to them until that realisation is made.

Remark Scope: the Hopf-spectator gate concerns the link residue, not a braid-level third-order winding number. For a braid on three strings z_1(t), z_2(t), z_3(t) in \mathbb{C}, Evans and Berger use Arnol'd's relation in the cohomology of the braid group to show that the one-form

They stress that it is well defined whether or not the net second-order winding numbers vanish; when they do vanish it agrees with the third-order linking number of the closed link [evans-berger1992, pp. 6--7].

It is not shown here to be a binding channel: whether \Psi_{ijk} is well defined on the corpus's braid words under its closure and basepoint conventions, and whether it has the right scale for a binding term, are both unchecked.

Remark The light-nucleus binding multiplicity is the coordination number of \mathcal{B}_K. The many-body binding weight of the jet-order filtration factorises as w_n(K) = M_n(A)\,\mathrm{Vol}_n(K), where \mathrm{Vol}_n(K) is the hyperbolic volume of the n-body sub-link of the building-block link \mathcal{B}_K and M_n(A) is a body-order multiplicity. The crossing/coordination structure of \mathcal{B}_K supplies a topological reading of M_n(A).

The multiplicity read off the crossing/coordination structure

Write the per-nucleon coordination number z(A) = A-1 (the number of nucleon–nucleon bonds incident to one nucleon in the fully coordinated cluster) and the total bond count C(A,2) = \tfrac{1}{2}A(A-1). Reading the required multiplicity straight off the AME2020 binding energies, M_{\mathrm{need}}(A) = B_{\mathrm{AME}} / (m_e\,\mathrm{Vol}_A):

{}^3\mathrm{H} 8_{11} 2.003 2
{}^3\mathrm{He} \mathrm{L6a4} (Borromean) 2.061 2
{}^4\mathrm{He} \mathrm{L6a4} base 7.557 3

For the non-magic A=3 pair the multiplicity is the per-nucleon coordination number z = A-1 = 2, matched to better than 3\% with no free parameter. The doubly-magic {}^4\mathrm{He} requires an additional factor M_{\mathrm{need}}/z = 2.5189, which is close to the super-exponential Schur–Weyl period a_D^{(4)} = \sum_{\lambda \vdash 4} \dim_q \lambda / 4 = 2.5328.

That period is derived, not read off the data: it is a q-dimension sum at the aether q_0 with no calibration and no free parameter, and its q = 1 limit is the exact rational I(4)/4 = 5/2 with I the involution numbers. The law M(A) = z(A)\,a_D^{(A)} is therefore fixed a priori and can be tested on every point. Tested, it fails: it over-shoots {}^3\mathrm{H} by 33.5\% and {}^3\mathrm{He} by 29.7\% — the \approx 30\% overshoot is this same law refuted one value of A down — and at {}^4\mathrm{He} it lands 0.55\% high, giving B({}^4\mathrm{He}) \approx 28.4517 MeV against the AME2020 value 28.2957 MeV. Restricting the factor to the magic shell is accordingly a selection between two parameter-free candidates rather than a derivation, and {}^4\mathrm{He} is the only nucleus in the volume-covered range A \le 4 that selects it. A window of width 0.028 about 2.5189 contains further parameter-free candidates, several of them closer than a_D^{(4)}, so the near-match does not single that period out. The Wigner-\mathrm{SU}(4) closed-shell structure cannot supply the factor either: the "at most four rows" restriction is satisfied by every partition of every n \le 4, so it leaves every Schur–Weyl sum below n = 5 unchanged and takes the same value at A = 3 and A = 4.

The deuteron sits on the Seifert-fibred Hopf link, where \mathrm{Vol} = 0 and any volume product vanishes. The crossing structure survives there — the Hopf link has crossing number 2, linking number |\mathrm{lk}| = 1, and per-nucleon coordination z = 1 — so the coordination carrier is the natural non-vanishing replacement for the volume on the two-body sub-link.

That the carrier is a coordination count and not a Gauss linking number is now proved rather than posited (the Brunnian binding channel). The {}^3\mathrm{He} and {}^4\mathrm{He} carriers are Borromean, hence Brunnian: every pairwise linking number vanishes, so a linking-number multiplier would read zero for exactly these nuclei. In the proved crossing-energy channel split the signed (linking-number) channel is empty for a Brunnian pair and the binding is carried by the sign-blind coordination-count channel, which is bar-odd and therefore complementary to the bar-even mass self-weight \mathrm{lw}. The deuteron Hopf case (\mathrm{lk} = z = 1) is the boundary where the two invariants coincide; they diverge at A \geq 3, where only the coordination count is non-vanishing.

Extension: \alpha-cluster coordination for A > 4

The heavier magic nuclei {}^{16}\mathrm{O} and {}^{40}\mathrm{Ca} are not single hyperbolic links but \alpha-conjugate clusters. The coordination principle lifts one level: treating each {}^4\mathrm{He} as one node and counting \alpha–\alpha coordination bonds,

  B(n_\alpha) \approx n_\alpha\,B({}^4\mathrm{He}) + N_{\mathrm{bonds}}\,b_{\alpha\alpha}.

For a simplex cluster (n_\alpha \le 4, complete \alpha-graph realisable up to the tetrahedron) N_{\mathrm{bonds}} = C(n_\alpha, 2), and the residual per bond is a near-constant b_{\alpha\alpha} \approx 2.41\,\text{MeV} ({}^{12}\mathrm{C}: 2.425; {}^{16}\mathrm{O}: 2.406). The closed-shell factor M_{\mathrm{need}}/z = 2.5189 is likewise an AME read; the Schur–Weyl period a_D^{(4)} = 2.5328 it is compared against is derived, but the identification of the two is not, as recorded above. The single \alpha–\alpha pair {}^8\mathrm{Be} gives \approx 0, consistent with its being unbound relative to two \alpha-particles. For n_\alpha \ge 5 the complete graph over-counts — not all pairs can be nearest neighbours in three dimensions — and the per-bond residual falls, so the coordination number saturates to a geometric close-packing count. That count is bounded by the three-dimensional kissing number 12: the touching pairs in any packing of n unit balls in \mathbb{E}^3 number fewer than 6n - 0.926\,n^{2/3} [bezdek-reid2013] (Thm.~1(i)), an affine bulk 12 \cdot n/2 minus a sub-affine surface deficit; the density statement behind the fcc picture is the Kepler theorem [hales-etal2010], which itself proves no contact bound. prop:binding-period-involution-statistic:
Proposition The balanced dimension sum is the involution generating function for 2\,\mathrm{maj} + \mathrm{content} \circ \mathrm{RSK}. For n \geq 1 let [k] = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) denote the balanced quantum integer, and for a partition \lambda \vdash n with hook lengths h(c), c \in \lambda, set

\dim_q^{\mathrm{bal}}(\lambda) \;=\; \frac{\prod_{k=1}^{n} [k]}{\prod_{c \in \lambda} [h(c)]},
\qquad
S^{\mathrm{bal}}(n; q) \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim_q^{\mathrm{bal}}(\lambda).

For an involution w \in \mathrm{Inv}(S_n) let \lambda(w) be its RSK shape, let \mathrm{maj}(w) = \sum_{i \in \mathrm{Des}(w)} i be its major index, where \mathrm{Des}(w) = \{\, i : w(i) > w(i+1) \,\} is the descent set, and let \mathrm{content}(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} (j - i) be the content sum of a shape. Then

S^{\mathrm{bal}}(n; q)\, q^{n(n-1)/2}
\;=\;
\sum_{w \in \mathrm{Inv}(S_n)} q^{\,2\,\mathrm{maj}(w) + \mathrm{content}(\lambda(w))} .

In particular both sides specialise at q = 1 to the involution count I(n). The common value is a polynomial in q of degree

\deg \;=\; n^{2} \;-\; H_{\min}(n),
\qquad
H_{\min}(n) \;=\; \min_{\lambda \vdash n} \sum_{c \in \lambda} h(c),

the minimum being over partitions of n of the total hook length. Writing T_k = k(k+1)/2, this minimum is itself closed-form,

H_{\min}(n) \;=\; 2n - 1 \;+\; \sum_{k \ge 2,\; T_k \le n-1} (n - T_k)
\;=\; \tfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\, n^{3/2} + O(n),

attained at the staircase (k, k-1, \dots, 1) when n = T_k is triangular, where it equals the square pyramidal number k(k+1)(2k+1)/6.

Proof Proof that the balanced dimension sum is the 2\,\mathrm{maj} + \mathrm{content} \circ \mathrm{RSK} involution generating function.   \cdot \frac{\prod_{k=1}^{n}[k]_{q^2}}{\prod_{c \in \lambda}[h(c)]_{q^2}}
= q^{\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda) - n(n-1)/2}\; \tilde f^{\lambda}(q^2).

Step 2 (q-hook-maj). Stanley's formula gives, for every \lambda \vdash n, \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} q^{\mathrm{maj}(T)} = \tilde f^{\lambda}(q) [stanley1999].

Step 3 (descent preservation on involutions). RSK restricts to a bijection w \mapsto P(w) from the involutions of RSK shape \lambda onto \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda), and \mathrm{Des}(w) = \mathrm{Des}(P(w)) (Schützenberger) [sagan2001]; hence \mathrm{maj}(w) = \mathrm{maj}(P(w)) and

\sum_{w \in \mathrm{Inv}(S_n),\; \lambda(w) = \lambda} q^{\,2\,\mathrm{maj}(w)}
= \tilde f^{\lambda}(q^2).

Multiplying by q^{\mathrm{content}(\lambda)}, summing over \lambda \vdash n, and applying Step 1 termwise yields \sum_{w} q^{2\,\mathrm{maj}(w) + \mathrm{content}(\lambda(w))} = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} q^{\mathrm{content}(\lambda)} \tilde f^{\lambda}(q^2) = q^{n(n-1)/2} S^{\mathrm{bal}}(n; q). The q = 1 specialisation counts the standard Young tableaux, \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} f^{\lambda} = I(n) with f^{\lambda} = \tilde f^{\lambda}(1) their number per shape. \blacksquare

Verification. For n = 3, 4 the identity is also proved by deciding the exponent multisets from the computable RSK insertion; exact symbolic verification for n \leq 8 (all 764 involutions at n = 8) has been carried out, and the transfer-operator reconstruction extends the exact cross-checks to n \leq 16 (hook side) and n \leq 24 (at q = 1).
